facts.fact: Kate 在门阶上守了一整天，越来越冷。
facts.anchor: Kate remained on the doorstep all day, growing progressively colder.

facts.fact: Smith 在电话里说这事很可疑，要设法被派到利兹陪她。
facts.anchor: ‘This sounds well dodgy. I’m going to get myself sent up there to be with you,’ he told her over the phone.

facts.fact: 两人的关系在同行中无人知晓，所以她在街上不能拥抱他。
facts.anchor: She couldn’t embrace him, because no one in their professional world knew of their relationship.

facts.fact: 和一群记者在一起时她觉得安全。
facts.anchor: Surrounded by the rest of the pack, she’d felt safe.

facts.fact: 独自走进酒店时，她突然觉得自己暴露在外。
facts.anchor: But here, a few minutes’ walk from the railway station, metres from the hotel’s tall arched entrance, its wrought-iron gates wide open, she felt suddenly exposed.

facts.fact: 她把匿名威胁解释成无聊的网络喷子，可这解释连她自己都不太信。
facts.anchor: A dumb troll, she told herself. A sad man sitting in his mum’s basement. But somehow it didn’t ring true.

facts.fact: 新闻首页上 Olivia 命案排在另一条脱欧新闻之下，让她厌烦。
facts.anchor: Olivia Kavanagh’s murder sat second from the top, beneath yet another Brexit story, the sight of which made her weary.

facts.fact: Kate 问 Smith 要不要为那条死亡威胁报警。
facts.anchor: ‘Do you think I should call the police?’

facts.fact: Smith 开玩笑说这案子是“性游戏出了岔子”。
facts.anchor: ‘I reckon it was a sex game gone wrong.’

facts.fact: Kate 立刻反驳：她是脖子被刺死的。
facts.anchor: ‘She was stabbed in the neck!’ exclaimed Kate

facts.fact: Smith 含糊地说“连谋杀都有它的好处”，心不在焉地亲了亲她的头顶。
facts.anchor: ‘Even murder has its upsides,’ he mumbled, kissing her absently on the top of her head.

facts.fact: 章末 Smith 说他有“一些主意”。
